answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted voting: every agent locks real collateral and influence follows the bond, not the headcount. Splitting one purse into a thousand fake agents does not shift the tide, because voting power still tracks locked capital. An attacker who fabricates a lagoon of dummy wallets pays a cost for each identity yet gains no extra weight; if any double-vote, the bond is slashed. The attack is a costly fable: the price is real locked funds plus forfeiture on detection, while honest agents only risk their own stake.
